In article <44h4gm$t...@newsbf02.news.aol.com> biom...@aol.com (Biomech8) writes:
>I was told that the only way you can use votes during a blood hunt is with
>votes provided by titles or by giving up the edge. This is this true?
>And
>if so what about the Ventrue Headquarters? The V:TES rulebook only states
>that you cannot block the vote or play reaction or action modifiers.

That's not true. You can use Ventrue HQ, and you can play PA's for
votes.

>Can someone please explain "vote pushing" to me? I see this term used
>quite often, yet I am unsure about it's meaning. Please take the time to
>enlighten me.

It concerns the suspected mis-rule on voting. There are three possible
interpretations of the voting rules in the rules booklet:

(1) Anybody can play any number of Political Action cards for
extra votes. This is called "vote pushing", and reportedly
distorts game balance. (Selfish vote decks become much powerful.)

(2) Only the non-calling Meth's can use PA cards for extra
votes.

(3) Each Meth can get (or play) at most one vote, including the
PA card used to call the vote, so the acting Meth. can't play
any more PA's and the others can play at most 1 PA each for a vote.
(I discovered this one.)

I recommend using either (2) or (3). Otherwise selfish vote decks
become way too annoying. (2) or (3) also encourages negotiated
vote decks, which makes the game more fun.

VH is okay. You may also throw down political action cards for votes.

>Can someone please explain "vote pushing" to me? I see this term used
>quite often, yet I am unsure about it's meaning. Please take the time to
>enlighten me.

"Vote pushing" refers to calling a vote, and then passing it by dropping

additional political actions from your hand. It seems very natural to
allow it, but permitting allows a certain class of weenie vote decks which
can normally pass anything they call until they run out of cards. Since
weenie decks have so many actions early on, this can make for a really
lethal, and pretty much unstoppable (stopped only by very unusual decks),
deck.

Literally read, the Jyhad rulebook forbids vote pushing (only *other*

Meths can drop extra political actions). The DT has said that is an error
and that you can push your own votes. I maintain that if it was a
mistake, it was an unusually fortuitous one.

This "fix" is simply inadequate. There are so many different PA cards,
you just ditch a variety of them to push whatever vote you want to

The political player is not hurt much by this rule. The various PA cards
are each quite powerful in its own respect. Varying the mix of PA cards
in his deck doesn't reduce much its power over non-voting decks,
as long as he can push the votes pass.

One vote per Meth!

"T.J. Hull" <t...@nwlink.com> writes:

>If a deck has an unusually high percentage of vote cards, it is
>vulnerable to:

> 1. Bleed decks, because it would have little intercept; and

> 2. Combat decks, due to lack of combat/protection cards; and

> 3. Intercept decks, owing to lack of stealth.

> After playing against a wide variety of opponents since the game's
>inception, I am convinced the game balances itself.

You're assuming that mostly-vote decks are still controlled by standard
mechanisms. The problem is that a weenie vote deck can often get around
all of the obstacles you mention. A weenie vote deck can cough up enough
votes to oust several Meths in the first vew turns. Combat deck (rush or
intercept) can generally get only vampire per turn until well into the
game and generally waits a turn or two before starting; the weenie voter
deck has 4-5 vampires out by turn two and pops out another almost every
turn (Effective Management). It beats a bleed deck because it's so fast
that it ousts faster than the bleeder.

If you don't think it works, you really should try one.

>

You don't need too many cards for bleed bounce. High percentage
of vote cards doesn't mean that you'll have few other cards in
your hand, since the vote cards cycle quickly. Bleeding him
just helps him oust his prey and cycle his hand.

> 2. Combat decks, due to lack of combat/protection cards; and

It doesn't take too many cards to S:CE either.

> 3. Intercept decks, owing to lack of stealth.

You intercept him, he S:CE with Majesty and untaps. Now you're
tapped, and he calls another vote. A weenie vote deck can vote
you out even without S:CE.

> After playing against a wide variety of opponents since the game's
>inception, I am convinced the game balances itself.

But a degenerate weenie vote deck did win a tournament.

Almost any deck has weaknesses; a deck having a "normal" degree of
weakness isn't an excuse for an overwhelming degree of power.

If the vote-pushing rules are `fixed', then a deck with a high
percentage of vote cards would really be weak, because he has
trouble getting the vote cards out of his hand. Now it's too
easy. One called vote and any number of vote cards can drop.
Almost no other cards are like that in Jyhad, except for of course
the mis-ruled Nimble Feet.

What do you define as "winning"? I personally consider getting 2VP in
a game as a "win" (3 VP would be 2 wins, etc.). I think weenie vote
decks are quite capable in that aspect.

> I would, however, like to see the rules ammended to only allow
>one political action card of a given type per vote per methuselah.
>Actually, a weenie bleed deck is almost as bad.... What I would really
>like to see is a master card that does, say, three damage to all vampires
>in play....

A weenie bleed deck is much lamer than a weenie vote deck. Weenie
bleed typically bleeds 2 pool per action (with Computer Hacking),
while weenie vote does 3 to prey and 1 to either predator or
grand-prey. Weenie bleed can also be countered by the (always
helpful) Telepathic Counter, or even by Deflection; there is virtually
nothing in the game to defend specifically against hostile votes,
except by grabbing a few votes yourself; hence there is nothing in
the game to defend against pushed votes.

I'd bet that your fix is /inadequate/. My proposal, of a max. of
1 Political Action card (regardless of type) per Meth. per vote
(and the caller has played his already, hasn't he), would be
more like it.

Another option to defending against hostile vote decks is Delaying Tactics.
While this isn't a particularly efficient option, you might be ok if you
could get down a Ventrue Headquarters and/or a couple of titles before
the vote deck gets to you. With that kind of preparation, the fact that they
can't take the Delayed political action again that turn would probably slow a
degenerate vote deck down enough for people to take it out, and could force
it out of cards if it needs too many cards to push the vote through.
Never experimented with this, though, and it'd be tricky to make the deck
general enough to take on non-political decks reliably.

What do you need to run a weenie vote deck? Weenies and a deck full of votes.

A combination that is easy, un-varied (monotonous) and works every time.
